seoTitle: Private Label Classic Sunglasses Sourcing Guide
seoDescription: Source private label classic sunglasses from China. Compare lens protection, optical quality, frames, hinges, fit, branding, cases and QC.
introduction: Classic Sunglasses can become a credible private-label offer when the product is defined around a real customer use rather than selected from a supplier photograph. Classic unisex frames can support fashion, travel, event and promotional ranges, but appearance alone does not establish lens protection, optical clarity, hinge durability or comfortable fit. Buyers should translate that opportunity into a written specification covering lens protection, optical quality, lens construction, frame material, packaging and batch consistency. Quotations should only be compared after suppliers confirm the same construction, test methods and branding scope, because a lower price may reflect a materially different product.
businessSummary: Sunglasses are compact, visually marketable and suitable for direct retail, boutiques, resorts, events and corporate campaigns; collections can expand through frame colours, lens treatments and cases without abandoning a recognisable silhouette. The strongest proposition gives the buyer a clear reason to choose this version and gives the brand enough control to reproduce the same experience on repeat orders. Commercial planning should include the intended sales channel, pack configuration, warranty or complaints policy, inspection cost and realistic landed-cost assumptions. A pre-production sample, approved artwork and measurable acceptance criteria are more valuable than broad claims such as “premium quality.”
marketNotes: Buyers compare face fit, weight, lens tint, frame finish, hinge feel and perceived protection. Low-priced promotional versions and everyday fashion eyewear should not be presented as equivalent when their materials and verified performance differ. Entry, mid-range and premium offers should be separated through measurable differences in lens protection, optical quality, lens construction, frame material, hinges and screws rather than through packaging language alone. Before committing to inventory, test the proposed product and price with the intended customer segment, compare competing pack sizes and identify the complaints that appear repeatedly in the category. Those findings should shape the supplier brief and the claims used on the final listing.
whiteLabelAngle: Use a recognisable frame-and-lens palette, restrained temple branding and protective packaging, while tying every protection or optical claim to evidence for the exact lens construction and production version. Practical customization options include Controlled frame colours with matching or contrasting lens tints; Laser, pad-print or metal temple logo; Polarized variant only where verified for the finished lens; Branded pouch, rigid case, cleaning cloth and retail sleeve. Keep the brand promise tied to features that can be inspected and repeated. Approve physical colour references, logo placement, packaging artwork, instructions and barcode data together with the product sample, then prohibit material or component substitutions without written approval. This creates a defensible range instead of a generic item carrying a new logo.
demandDrivers: Sun exposure creates an everyday functional use alongside fashion demand.
Eyewear is highly visible and supports strong lifestyle branding.
Compact products suit boutiques, events, resorts and ecommerce fulfilment.
Cases, pouches and cleaning cloths create straightforward bundles.
targetBuyers: Fashion boutiques and online accessory stores
Lifestyle brands serving students and urban professionals

specifications.label: Lens protection
specifications.guidance: Define required UV performance and obtain test evidence tied to the exact lens material, colour and coating.

specifications.label: Optical quality
specifications.guidance: Control refractive power, prism, distortion, haze and visible defects across the useful lens area.

specifications.label: Lens construction
specifications.guidance: Specify material, base curve, thickness, tint, category, polarization if claimed and scratch-resistant treatment.

specifications.label: Frame material
specifications.guidance: Define the polymer or metal construction, colour, finish, flexibility, weight and resistance to sweat and corrosion.

specifications.label: Hinges and screws
specifications.guidance: Approve hinge type, opening force, screw retention, cycle durability and alignment of both temples.

specifications.label: Fit dimensions
specifications.guidance: State lens width, bridge, temple length, total frame width, pantoscopic alignment and allowed tolerances.

specifications.label: Surface and branding
specifications.guidance: Control scratches, sink marks, sharp edges, logo method, placement, colour and abrasion resistance.

specifications.label: Case and labelling
specifications.guidance: Define pouch or case, cleaning cloth, warnings, traceability, barcode and protection during transport.

sourcingRisks.title: Unverified protection claims
sourcingRisks.guidance: A dark lens is not evidence of UV performance; claims must match testing for the production lens.

sourcingRisks.title: Optical distortion
sourcingRisks.guidance: Poor moulding and lens control can cause visual discomfort even when the frame looks acceptable.

sourcingRisks.title: Weak hinges
sourcingRisks.guidance: Loose screws, brittle temples and inconsistent opening force lead to early breakage and returns.

sourcingRisks.title: Batch colour variation
sourcingRisks.guidance: Frame resin, coatings and lens tint can shift between sample and production without controlled references.

shippingNotes: Frames and lenses can scratch, twist or break when units move inside weak packaging. Hold temples in the intended position, isolate lenses from abrasive surfaces and prevent master cartons from placing bending loads on retail boxes or cases. Obtain the final individual pack size, master-carton dimensions, units per carton, gross weight and stacking arrangement from a production-equivalent branded sample before confirming freight. Packaging should protect the product through compression, vibration, moisture and handling appropriate to the route. Recheck carton markings, batch traceability, quantities and product condition before release, and calculate landed cost from the approved packed configuration rather than an early supplier estimate.

faqs.question: Can classic sunglasses be private labelled?
faqs.answer: Yes. The product can be differentiated through controlled colours, construction, branding and packaging. Approve the complete branded sample and record the specification before mass production rather than treating logo application as the only private-label decision.

faqs.question: What specifications matter when sourcing classic sunglasses?
faqs.answer: The core specification should cover lens protection, optical quality, lens construction, frame material, hinges and screws, fit dimensions, plus branding, pack configuration, tolerances, inspection method and batch traceability. The exact priorities should follow the intended customer and use case.

faqs.question: How should suppliers for classic sunglasses be compared?
faqs.answer: Send every shortlisted supplier the same written brief and ask for a production-equivalent sample. Compare confirmed construction, test evidence, quality controls, packaging capability, change-control process and response to defects—not the headline quotation alone.

faqs.question: What should be checked before approving a production sample?
faqs.answer: Check dimensions, materials, functional performance, workmanship, colour, odour where relevant, logo durability, packaging, instructions and the claims printed on the pack. Retain the signed sample as the inspection reference.

faqs.question: What are the main sourcing risks for classic sunglasses?
faqs.answer: Important risks include unverified protection claims, optical distortion, weak hinges, batch colour variation. Convert each risk into a specification, supplier question or inspection checkpoint before the purchase order is placed.

faqs.question: How should classic sunglasses be prepared for shipping?
faqs.answer: Frames and lenses can scratch, twist or break when units move inside weak packaging. Hold temples in the intended position, isolate lenses from abrasive surfaces and prevent master cartons from placing bending loads on retail boxes or cases. Confirm the final packed dimensions and test the shipping configuration before using it for freight and landed-cost calculations.
